CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION adempiere.paymenttermduedate(paymentterm_id numeric, docdate timestamp with time zone)
 RETURNS timestamp with time zone
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 STABLE
AS $function$
/*************************************************************************
 * The contents of this file are subject to the Compiere License.  You may
 * obtain a copy of the License at    http://www.compiere.org/license.html
 * Software is on an  "AS IS" basis,  WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND, either
 * express or implied. See the License for details. Code: Compiere ERP+CRM
 * Copyright (C) 1999-2001 Jorg Janke, ComPiere, Inc. All Rights Reserved.
 *
 * converted to postgreSQL by Karsten Thiemann (Schaeffer AG), 
 * kthiemann@adempiere.org
 *************************************************************************
 * Title:	Get Due timestamp with time zone
 * Description:
 *	Returns the due timestamp with time zone
 * Test:
 *	select paymenttermDueDate(106, now()) from Test; => now()+30 days
 ************************************************************************/
DECLARE
 	Days				NUMERIC := 0;
	DueDate				timestamp with time zone := TRUNC(DocDate);
	--
	FirstDay			timestamp with time zone;
	NoDays				NUMERIC;
	p   			RECORD;
BEGIN
	FOR p IN 
		SELECT	*
		FROM	C_PaymentTerm
		WHERE	C_PaymentTerm_ID = PaymentTerm_ID
	LOOP	--	for convineance only
		--	Due 15th of following month
		IF (p.IsDueFixed = 'Y') THEN		
			FirstDay := TRUNC(DocDate, 'MM');
			NoDays := EXTRACT(day FROM TRUNC(DocDate) - FirstDay);
			DueDate := FirstDay + (p.FixMonthDay-1);	--	starting on 1st
			DueDate := ADD_MONTHS(DueDate, p.FixMonthOffset);
			IF (NoDays > p.FixMonthCutoff) THEN
				DueDate := ADD_MONTHS(DueDate, 1);
			END IF;
		ELSE
			DueDate := TRUNC(DocDate) + p.NetDays;
		END IF;
	END LOOP;
	RETURN DueDate;
END;
$function$
```

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION adempiere.trunc(datetime timestamp without time zone, format character varying)
 RETURNS date
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 IMMUTABLE
AS $function$
BEGIN
	IF format = 'Q' THEN
		RETURN CAST(DATE_Trunc('quarter',datetime) as DATE);
	ELSIF format = 'Y' or format = 'YEAR' THEN
		RETURN CAST(DATE_Trunc('year',datetime) as DATE);
	ELSIF format = 'MM' or format = 'MONTH' THEN
		RETURN CAST(DATE_Trunc('month',datetime) as DATE);
	ELSIF format = 'DD' THEN
		RETURN CAST(DATE_Trunc('day',datetime) as DATE);
	ELSIF format = 'DY' THEN
		RETURN CAST(DATE_Trunc('day',datetime) as DATE);
	ELSE
		RETURN CAST(datetime AS DATE);
	END IF;
END;
$function$
```

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION adempiere.adddays(datetime timestamp with time zone, days numeric)
 RETURNS timestamp with time zone
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 IMMUTABLE
AS $function$
BEGIN
	if datetime is null or days is null then
		return null;
	end if;
	return datetime + (interval '1' second * (86400 * days));
END;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION adempiere.adddays(inter interval, days numeric)
 RETURNS integer
 LANGUAGE plpgsql
 IMMUTABLE
AS $function$
BEGIN   
RETURN ( EXTRACT( EPOCH FROM ( inter ) ) / 86400 ) + days;
END;

  Rows come in primary-key order with typed values (numeric -> Decimal, timestamp -> naive datetime,

  Filter anything else in Python. Available tables and columns:
  - c_paymentterm: c_paymentterm_id, isduefixed, netdays, fixmonthcutoff, fixmonthday, fixmonthoffset
- `data.session_tz` is the PostgreSQL session TimeZone as a tzinfo. Legacy date logic (casts to date,
  TRUNC, interval and day arithmetic) happens in that zone. Python adds timedelta to an aware datetime
  in wall-clock time; PostgreSQL's `+ interval '1 second' * n` adds elapsed time. They differ across
  daylight-saving changes.

- PostgreSQL numeric arithmetic is exact and ROUND(numeric, n) rounds half away from zero; Python's
  default decimal context has 28 digits and banker's rounding.

## Task
Write the module. Put any assumption you could not confirm from the source in `notes`.

response.notes:
The port follows the source and the spec. I traced two of the golden cases by hand (e-8b16f38f7228, the March DST cutoff case, and e-1906c08077a7) and they match. I did not run the module against the full set of golden cases.

Assumptions I couldn't confirm from the source:
- Ambiguous and nonexistent local times. I assumed PostgreSQL always takes the later UTC instant. My port tries both fold values and keeps the later result. For a nonexistent time (spring forward) that means the pre-change standard offset; for an ambiguous one (fall back) it means standard time.
- Fractional days. Days are added as 86400*N seconds: an exact Decimal product, then converted to float, multiplied by 1e6 and rounded half-to-even to whole microseconds. I believe this matches how PostgreSQL rounds interval * float8.
- NoDays. This is the whole-day part of the elapsed microseconds between the two dates, truncated toward zero. That is my model of justify_hours followed by EXTRACT(day).
- Month offset. FixMonthOffset is truncated toward zero with int(Decimal). When adding months, the local wall-clock time is kept and the day is clamped to the end of the month. The cutoff month is added as a separate step, so clamping can happen twice.
- IsDueFixed. Trailing spaces are stripped before comparing, matching how PostgreSQL compares character(1). Otherwise only an exact 'Y' selects the fixed branch.
- More than one matching row. The last row wins, as in the legacy loop. In practice there can't be more than one because the column is the primary key.
- NULL docdate returns None.
